questions.stem:
Statements: U > Q = R < X < W.
Conclusions: I. R > U   II. W ≥ X.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is definitely true. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
banking credit savings = ni ka ze
banking growth secure = ni su lu
credit growth rural = lu ze re
savings secure rural = su ka re
banking credit rural = ni ze re
What is the code for “growth”?
questions.explanation: Answer: lu. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: banking = ni, credit = ze, savings = ka, growth = lu, secure = su, rural = re.

questions.stem:
Statements: Some branches are loans. All loans are coins. No coins is a bonds.
Conclusions:
I. Some branches are coins.
II. Some loans are bonds.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few branches are loans. Some loans are coins. All coins are bonds.
Conclusions:
I. All branches are bonds.
II. No loans is a bonds.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few branches are loans. All loans are coins. No coins is a bonds.
Conclusions:
I. Some branches are not loans.
II. No loans is a bonds.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:
Statements: No branches is a loans. Some loans are coins. All coins are bonds.
Conclusions:
I. All branches are bonds.
II. Some bonds are loans.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 109 km south, turns right and walks 204 km, then turns right and walks 24 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 221. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 85 km along the initial direction and 204 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(85² + 204²) = 221 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 70 km east, turns left and walks 72 km, then turns left and walks 16 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?

questions.stem: C is the brother of G. G is the mother of B. F is the father of C and G. How is C related to B?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. C is the brother of B’s mother G. Therefore C is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: B is the only daughter of F. F is the father of B. E is the son of B. G is the sister of F. How is F related to E?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. F is the father of B, and B is E’s mother. Thus F is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: E is the mother of A. F is the daughter of A. D is the father of A. How is F related to D?
questions.explanation: Answer: Granddaughter. D is a parent of A, and F is A’s daughter. Hence F is D’s grandchild.

questions.stem: In a queue of 64 candidates, a candidate is 11th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 51. New front rank = 11+3 = 14. Back rank = 64 − 14 + 1 = 51.

questions.stem: In a queue of 46 candidates, a candidate is 12th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 31. New front rank = 12+4 = 16. Back rank = 46 − 16 + 1 = 31.

questions.stem: A is twice as old as B. After 20 years their ages will be in ratio 3:2. What is the present sum of their ages?
questions.explanation: Answer: 60. Let B = x, A = 2x. (2x+20)/(x+20) = 3/2 gives x = 20. Present sum = 3x.

questions.stem: A sum of ₹21000 earns ₹3150 simple interest in 3 years. At the same annual rate, what would be the amount (₹) after 2 years with annual compounding? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)

questions.stem: A container holds 120 litres of pure milk. 24 litres are removed and replaced with water. This process is repeated once more, mixing thoroughly each time. How many litres of milk remain? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)

questions.stem: Two articles are sold for ₹2700 each. One earns 25% profit and the other incurs 25% loss. Find the combined cost price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 5760. Recover each cost separately: 2700×100/125 + 2700×100/75. Equal selling prices do not imply equal costs.

questions.stem: A and B invest in ratio 7:5. A invests for 12 months; B joins later and invests for 7 months. A receives ₹134400 profit. What is the total profit (₹)?
questions.explanation: Answer: 190400. Profit ratio is 84:35. Each ratio unit = ₹1600. Total = 119 × 1600.

questions.stem: The average weight of 13 people is 35 kg. One person joins and the average rises by 1 kg. Find the new person’s weight (kg).
questions.explanation: Answer: 49. New total minus old total = (13+1)×(35+1) − 13×35 = 49.

questions.stem: The price of a commodity increases by 25%. A household keeps spending fixed at ₹1900. By what percentage must consumption decrease? (Round to two decimals.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 20. New quantity / old quantity = 100/125. Reduction percentage = 25/125 ×100.

questions.stem: Two inlet pipes can fill a tank in 38 and 57 hours. An outlet empties it in 76 hours. All three open together. Find the time (hours) to fill the empty tank. (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 32.57. Net rate = 1/38 + 1/57 − 1/76 = 7/228 tank/hour. Required time = 32.57 hours.
